_readme: Anchor statement sets for Semantic Similarity Rating (Maier et al. 2025, arXiv:2510.08338).
Each set is five statements forming a gradient from Likert 1 (intent improbable) to 5 (intent probable).
Index 0 = Likert 1, index 4 = Likert 5. A free-text response is embedded and compared to all five;
the resulting distributions are averaged across every set for the construct.
Design principles, from the paper's Appendix C.1: keep them short, generic and domain-independent
so they apply to any concept; the lowest anchor expresses that the purchase is unlikely, the middle
anchor indifference or uncertainty, the highest anchor intent to purchase; the two intermediate
anchors sit semantically between their neighbours. Multiple sets exist because wording measurably
shifts the mapping, and averaging over phrasings is what stops any one set's idiom from driving
the result. The paper used six sets for purchase intent and three for a secondary construct.
These sets are written from those principles and are NOT fitted to this business's real data.
See references/calibration.md for how to fit them once real inquiry outcomes exist.
